bull.b: Rapid growth and contracted server demand provide a clearer route to scale than pilot activity alone. The expected ~$50M committed backlog entering 2027 can support production planning and customer diversification, although execution remains essential.

bull.t: Low leverage and improved equity position
bull.b: Minimal debt reduces refinancing and interest burdens, while the return to positive equity improves financial resilience. This gives Blaize more flexibility to fund commercialization than a highly leveraged structure, though ongoing losses can erode that cushion.

bull.t: Diversified AI product and software strategy
bull.b: A model spanning embedded silicon and SDKs, cloud and data-center platforms, and planned AI Services can diversify revenue and create repeatable software contribution. If adoption develops, higher-margin services may improve mix and reduce dependence on hardware economics.

bear.b: The reset indicates customer conversions and procurement are taking materially longer than planned, weakening near-term revenue visibility. Delayed deployments can defer cash receipts, slow scale benefits, and make the 2027 growth plan more dependent on successful execution.

Low and volatile gross margins limit operating leverage and make growth less valuable until product mix improves. Reliance on lower-margin third-party server hardware and persistent memory inflation could prolong pressure on profitability and weaken the path to breakeven.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and continuing losses
bear.b: Sustained negative free cash flow means Blaize must continue funding operations while scaling, increasing dependence on financing or customer advances. The large EBITDA loss also reduces the likelihood that current growth will soon become self-funding, creating dilution and liquidity risk.
